content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term, especially after recent spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true value by 1–3% in the first 5–10 days post-forecast, then gradually converge.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the early part of the 30-day window, especially when true values show a sharp drop or correction.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum when recent 7–14 day average is falling; tends to ignore short-term mean reversion.
- When true values show a strong upward trend, model often lags by 1–3 days and then overcorrects.
- Model overreacts to recent high values, leading to artificial peaks in forecast, especially if last 5–7 days are high.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if the true value is below the 30-day moving average of the history, especially if the model is above it.
- Model tends to ignore the influence of the 7-day moving average in the forecast, leading to persistent bias in the middle of the forecast horizon.
- When true values show a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to adjust and continues to forecast higher than true.
